Control ac-2.1 is in control ac-2 and has a part with the name bogus. The target query of oscal-control-statement-part-name selects that part from each ancestor control, and the entry still gives one failure. Every control has a statement part, so the entry oscal-catalog-control-require-statement-when-appropriate does not fail. The input is adapted and trimmed from AC-2 and AC-2(1) of the SP 800-53 rev5 catalog in usnistgov/oscal-content at commit 78650f02ad9321bb7b817846f8fbd4f2bcd620de.

Control ac-2.1.1 is in control ac-2.1, which is in control ac-2, and has a part with the name bogus. The target query of oscal-control-statement-part-name selects that part from each of the three ancestor controls, and the entry still gives one failure. Every control has a statement part, so the entry oscal-catalog-control-require-statement-when-appropriate does not fail. The input is adapted and trimmed from AC-2 and AC-2(1) of the SP 800-53 rev5 catalog in usnistgov/oscal-content at commit 78650f02ad9321bb7b817846f8fbd4f2bcd620de. SP 800-53 has no third level, so control ac-2.1.1 is synthetic.

The entry oscal-activity-type-values is closed and lists the values INTERVIEW, EXAMINE and TEST. The method prop of the activity has the value test. This value differs from the listed value TEST only in case, and the entry gives one failure. The input is a copy of documents/invalid/constraints/oscal-activity-type-values.json with the value test in place of zz-invalid.
The start is the later calendar date in its own offset, and the end is the earlier one.
Two values share one instant. The outer task comes first in document order.
Both bounds come from the second result. A binding that keeps six fraction digits sees equal instants.

The tasks are not in date order. The start comes from an on-date of the second task, so a binding that takes the first start in document order gives 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z. The end comes from a within-date-range of a nested task in the first task, so a binding that takes the last end in document order gives the on-date 2026-01-15T08:00:00Z, and a binding that skips nested tasks gives 2026-02-28T00:00:00Z. The at-frequency timing of the third task gives no datetime. The input is synthetic.
A task and its nested task have only at-frequency timing, so both bounds are empty. The value null stands for an empty bound. The input is synthetic.
The only task has an on-date, which is both the start and the end. The offset stays as written. The input is synthetic.
A property name is a token, and a token has no spaces.

The element is a list of two mappings. The second mapping has a property with the name bogus. The location of the failure is the second item of the list, `$[0][1]`, followed by the rest of the location in that item.
The value has 63 hexadecimal digits, and SHA-256 needs 64.
The element cannot hold the party that its party identifier names, so the element has no constraint failure.

The value has 63 hexadecimal digits, and the default algorithm SHA-256 needs 64.
The YAML parse operation gets the raw bytes of the input, not text. The input is the same file as the input of yaml-round-trip/catalog.
The YAML parse-from-file operation gets the path of the input. The input is the same file as the input of yaml-round-trip/profile.
Plain scalars at string locations keep their text: 1.0, 1.10, yes, null, ~, an empty scalar, and a datetime with seven fraction digits. The !!int tag and the !!omap tag do not change a value.

The quoted "443" and the plain 443.0 at port-range locations are the number 443. The alias *port at a property value is the string "443". The metadata version "1.0" stays a string after serialization.

The catalog has only its required fields, so every optional field is absent. A serializer that writes an absent field as null gives the string "null" at a string location and a parse error at any other location (YML-004.04), so the second parse of the round trip fails. A serializer that writes an absent field as an empty value passes the round trip, so the runner also reads the serialized YAML as generic YAML and checks that none of the keys in expected-absent-keys occurs. The input is the YAML form of documents/valid/minimal-catalog.json.
The plain scalar true at the as-is location is the boolean true.
The input is a valid Profile in YAML, and the typed parser is for a Catalog. The input is the same file as the input of yaml-round-trip/profile.
The flow sequence of props has no closing bracket. Reader fault: `syntax`.
A --- line separates two minimal catalogs. Reader fault: `two-documents`.
The stream holds only a comment. Reader fault: `no-document`.
The minimal catalog in UTF-16 with a byte order mark. Reader fault: `not-utf-8`.
The metadata holds the key title two times. Reader fault: `duplicate-key`.
The metadata holds the plain key title and the quoted key "title", which have the same text. Reader fault: `duplicate-key`.
A key of the metadata is a sequence. Reader fault: `non-scalar-key`.
The back-matter anchored as &bm holds the alias *bm. Reader fault: `alias-cycle`.
The metadata holds the key << with an alias to a property. The key is an ordinary key, so it is a field that the schema does not define. Reader fault: `schema`.
The metadata holds colour, a field that the schema does not define. Reader fault: `schema`.
The as-is location takes a boolean, and yes is not true or false. Reader fault: `grammar`.
The start location takes a number, and 0x1BB does not match the JSON number grammar. Reader fault: `grammar`.
The start location takes a number, and the JSON number grammar has no plus sign. Reader fault: `grammar`.

The second control has the id ac-2, and so has a control inside the first control. A selection in the order of the query gives the second control before the inner control, and the failure is at the inner control. The order of the locations puts the inner control first, so the failure is at the second control.

The catalog gives the member groups before the member controls. A part in the first group and a part in the first control have the id ac_smt. By code point, controls comes before groups, so the failure is at the part in the group.

The controls at the indexes 2 and 10 have the id ac-3. The index 2 comes before the index 10, so the failure is at the control at the index 10. An order of the text of the locations puts the index 10 first.
